requirement:
Per-file annotation details in the coverage overview are collapsed
initially.
rationale:
structural: The text of `requirements.test-coverage.index.gaps.details.initial` is: "Per-file annotation details in the coverage overview are collapsed initially." It states one observable property of the rendered overview: the details start collapsed. It names no library, type, signature, algorithm or delegation interface.

Any implementation that renders the details collapsed satisfies it. A native `<details>` element without `open` would do. So would a script that collapses the sections on load, or a CSS rule that hides them. All of these give the same observable result, so how the collapse is built is discretionary.

The requirement has no implementation edges and no review roots were supplied. With no structural obligation, no implementation root needs a reference.

behavioral: The requirement has one observable obligation: per-file annotation details in the coverage overview start collapsed.

`src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[documented_items_are_counted_once_with_browsable_directory_and_file_groups]` renders an overview with several files: a root file, files in nested directories, and one outside `src`. For `code.rs`, `src/direct.rs` and `src/deep/nested.rs`, it takes each file's card with `file_card`. The card includes the file row and its detail row. It asserts that the card contains `aria-expanded="false"` and ` hidden>`. It also asserts that the file's summary row is not hidden, so only the details are collapsed. These assertions check the initial collapsed state for each file with annotations, whether at the root, directly in a directory, or nested.

The same test asserts that the directory groups are `open`. That is a different requirement, `index.file_map.directories.initial`, and is not judged here.

`src/execution_coverage/check.rs#mod[tests]/fn[book_browses_all_proposals_while_cli_checks_reviews_and_measurements]` renders the real page and calls `exercise_file_click`. That helper takes the emitted button, with `aria-expanded="false"` and the detail rows hidden, and runs its handler in Node. It confirms the initial state is collapsed and can be expanded. It is supporting evidence.

Both tests carry `{test}` markers for the subject. I found no unmarked relevant tests and no untested obligation.
